Problem 2 — a galaxy given a shove, and why it stops

Work with k=0k=0k=0 in comoving Cartesian coordinates, so that ds2=c2dt2−a2(t)(dX2+dY2+dZ2)\dd s^{2}=c^{2}\dd t^{2}-a^{2}(t)\big(\dd X^{2}+\dd Y^{2}+\dd Z^{2}\big)ds2=c2dt2−a2(t)(dX2+dY2+dZ2). (a) Identify a Killing vector by inspection and write down the conserved charge of Chapter 3.5 §9 for a massive particle. (b) Deduce that the particle's momentum as measured by the comoving observer it is passing falls as 1/a1/a1/a. (c) Show that this reproduces §5.1's photon result in the limit v→cv\to cv→c, and explain in one sentence why the two cases had to agree. (d) Our own peculiar velocity relative to the microwave background is 370 km s−1370\ \mathrm{km\,s^{-1}}370 kms−1 (§1.2). If everything else stopped acting, what would it be when the universe is ten times its present size? What does the answer say about the state a galaxy settles into?

Solution

(a) The metric components do not mention XXX, so by Chapter 3.5 §8.1's practical test ξμ=(0,1,0,0)\xi^{\mu}=(0,1,0,0)ξμ=(0,1,0,0) is a Killing vector, and by (3.9.7)'s gXX=−a2g_{XX}=-a^{2}gXX​=−a2 the charge is

Q  =  ξμuμ  =  gXX uX  =  −a2 uX  =  constant. Q \;=\; \xi_{\mu}u^{\mu} \;=\; g_{XX}\,u^{X} \;=\; -a^{2}\,u^{X} \;=\; \text{constant}. Q=ξμ​uμ=gXX​uX=−a2uX=constant.

Three such charges, one per direction. They are the same three Killing vectors §1.1 called homogeneity, now doing work.

(b) The proper distance moved per unit proper time, as measured locally, is a dX/dτ=a uXa\,\dd X/\dd\tau=a\,u^{X}adX/dτ=auX, and the momentum per unit mass is that same quantity. From (a), uX=−Q/a2u^{X}=-Q/a^{2}uX=−Q/a2, so

∣p∣  =  m a ∣uX∣  =  m∣Q∣a  ∝  1a. \abs{p} \;=\; m\,a\,\abs{u^{X}} \;=\; \frac{m\abs{Q}}{a} \;\propto\; \frac{1}{a}. ∣p∣=ma​uX​=am∣Q∣​∝a1​.

(c) For light, §5.1 found p0∝1/ap^{0}\propto1/ap0∝1/a and hence hν∝1/ah\nu\propto1/ahν∝1/a. Since a photon's energy is ccc times its momentum, its momentum also falls as 1/a1/a1/a. The two agree because the derivations differ only in which normalisation was imposed, and neither used the normalisation at the step where the 1/a1/a1/a appeared. Physically: momentum decays as 1/a1/a1/a for everything, and only the relation between momentum and energy distinguishes the cases.

(d) 370/10=37 km s−1370/10=37\ \mathrm{km\,s^{-1}}370/10=37 kms−1. Peculiar motion decays. A galaxy given any kick coasts asymptotically to comoving rest without anything acting on it. That is why §5.3's "at rest in comoving coordinates" is not a special initial condition but an attractor, and why the comoving frame is a physically distinguished one even though nothing in the field equations distinguishes a slicing. In reality gravitational infall towards nearby masses keeps regenerating peculiar velocities, and 370 km s−1370\ \mathrm{km\,s^{-1}}370 kms−1 is what that competition currently produces.

Step 3 of §6.2 divided by dR/dx0\dd R/\dd x^{0}dR/dx0, which is zero here, so the argument yields nothing, and correctly so, since the conclusion is false.

(d) Two honest halves. Yes, locally and for test bodies: inside rˉ<c/H\bar r\lt c/Hrˉ<c/H the charge ξμpμ\xi_{\mu}p^{\mu}ξμ​pμ is conserved along every geodesic by Chapter 3.5 §9, so a photon crossing the static patch has a well-defined conserved energy and Chapter 3.8 §5's machinery applies unchanged. No, as a statement about the universe: the patch is a region and not the spacetime, every comoving observer has a different one, and de Sitter space contains no matter to have an energy in the first place. Adding any dust at all destroys the Killing vector by §6.2, and the real universe is 31.5%31.5\%31.5% dust.

Problem 4 — Friedmann from Newton, and the three things it cannot see

A famous coincidence: Friedmann's first equation can be obtained without any general relativity at all. (a) Take a uniform ball of dust of density ρ(t)\rho(t)ρ(t) and radius R(t)R(t)R(t), and a test particle on its surface. Write down Newtonian energy conservation for that particle and rearrange it into the form of (3.9.10). What plays the part of −kc2-kc^{2}−kc2? (b) Two objections should occur to you. The ball has an edge and the universe does not, and matter outside the ball ought to count for something. Say which results from Chapters 3.7 and 0.7 answer each. (c) Now find the failures. Show that the same argument gives R¨=−GM/R2\ddot R=-GM/R^{2}R¨=−GM/R2 and hence an acceleration equation without the pressure term. For which of §4.1's three fluids does that give the wrong answer, and by how much? (d) Show that the Newtonian argument also forces ρ∝a−3\rho\propto a^{-3}ρ∝a−3 and therefore cannot describe radiation at all, and say in one sentence what the a−4a^{-4}a−4 requires that Newton does not have.

Solution

(a) Mass enclosed M=43πR3ρM=\tfrac43\pi R^{3}\rhoM=34​πR3ρ, constant if the dust moves with the surface. Energy per unit mass: 12R˙2−GM/R=E\half\dot R^{2}-GM/R=\mathcal{E}21​R˙2−GM/R=E, a constant. Multiply by 2/R22/R^{2}2/R2:

(R˙R)2  =  2GMR3+2ER2  =  8πGρ3+2ER2, \left(\frac{\dot R}{R}\right)^{2} \;=\; \frac{2GM}{R^{3}} + \frac{2\mathcal{E}}{R^{2}} \;=\; \frac{8\pi G\rho}{3} + \frac{2\mathcal{E}}{R^{2}}, (RR˙​)2=R32GM​+R22E​=38πGρ​+R22E​,

which is (3.9.10) with RRR for aaa and 2E=−kc22\mathcal{E}=-kc^{2}2E=−kc2. A bound ball (E<0\mathcal{E}\lt0E<0) corresponds to k=+1k=+1k=+1 and recollapses, an unbound one to k=−1k=-1k=−1, and the marginal case to k=0k=0k=0. That is why the closed universe of Problem 1 is the one that turns round.

(b) The edge: Chapter 3.7 §4's Birkhoff theorem says the geometry outside any spherical distribution depends only on the mass inside, and ⚑ its interior counterpart, quoted rather than proved, says a spherical shell contributes nothing to the field inside it. So the ball may be taken as a piece cut from a homogeneous universe and the rest ignored. Chapter 0.7 §8 derived the same statement for the inverse-square law from the divergence theorem. Only the enclosed source appears, and a hollow shell exerts no force inside itself, which it named as Newton's shell theorem. Both give the same licence, and Birkhoff is the reason the Newtonian licence survives into general relativity.

(c) Differentiating the energy equation, or directly from F=ma\vv F=m\vv aF=ma, R¨=−GM/R2=−4πG3ρR\ddot R=-GM/R^{2}=-\tfrac{4\pi G}{3}\rho RR¨=−GM/R2=−34πG​ρR. Compare (3.9.13): the bracket ρ+3p/c2\rho+3p/c^{2}ρ+3p/c2 has become ρ\rhoρ alone. For dust that is exact and the Newtonian answer is right. For radiation, p=ρc2/3p=\rho c^{2}/3p=ρc2/3 makes the true bracket 2ρ2\rho2ρ, so the Newtonian version underestimates the deceleration by a factor of two. For the cosmological term the true bracket is −2ρ-2\rho−2ρ and the Newtonian one is +ρ+\rho+ρ: the sign is wrong, so a Newtonian argument predicts that vacuum energy attracts, and the entire late-time behaviour of the universe is invisible to it.

(d) The Newtonian argument holds M=43πR3ρM=\tfrac43\pi R^{3}\rhoM=34​πR3ρ fixed, which is ρ∝R−3\rho\propto R^{-3}ρ∝R−3 by construction, so it cannot produce any other dilution law. Getting a−4a^{-4}a−4 requires the energy of each quantum to fall as 1/a1/a1/a, which is §5.1's null-geodesic result, and Newtonian gravity has no null geodesics and no reason for light to respond to gravity at all. So the coincidence in (a) is genuine but narrow: it works for pressureless matter, which is exactly the case in which relativity has nothing new to say.

The brick you just laid — and the wall Part III has finished

The metric was forced, not chosen. Two symmetry assumptions do all of it: no special place, no special direction, six Killing fields between them. They fix g00=1g_{00}=1g00​=1 and g0i=0g_{0i}=0g0i​=0 by inspection, reduce the spatial geometry to one of constant curvature, and turn that condition into a single separable equation. Its solution, made regular at the origin, is dℓ2=dr2/(1−kr2)+r2dΩ2\dd\ell^{2}=\dd r^{2}/(1-kr^{2})+r^{2}\dd\Omega^{2}dℓ2=dr2/(1−kr2)+r2dΩ2 with kkk of one of three signs. One function a(t)a(t)a(t) survives. And kkk is a statement about curvature rather than about whether space is finite, which is the fifth appearance in this book of a local fact failing to determine a global one.

Two equations, and the third for free. G00G_{00}G00​ gives (a˙/a)2=8πGρ/3−kc2/a2(\dot a/a)^{2}=8\pi G\rho/3-kc^{2}/a^{2}(a˙/a)2=8πGρ/3−kc2/a2. The 111111 component gives a¨/a=−4πG3(ρ+3p/c2)\ddot a/a=-\tfrac{4\pi G}{3}(\rho+3p/c^{2})a¨/a=−34πG​(ρ+3p/c2), but only once Friedmann I has been substituted into it. And dI/dx0−2a′II\dd\mathrm{I}/\dd x^{0}-2a'\mathrm{II}dI/dx0−2a′II is exactly −8πGa2/3c2-8\pi Ga^{2}/3c^{2}−8πGa2/3c2 times the fluid equation. That is Chapter 3.4's contracted Bianchi identity and Chapter 3.6's cornering, met a third time and now as arithmetic. The one static solution, ρm=2ρΛ\rho_{\text{m}}=2\rho_{\Lambda}ρm​=2ρΛ​ with k=+1k=+1k=+1 and aE=1/Λa_{\text{E}}=1/\sqrt\LambdaaE​=1/Λ​, perturbs to ε¨=+Λc2ε\ddot\varepsilon=+\Lambda c^{2}\varepsilonε¨=+Λc2ε and falls over on a ten-billion-year timescale, which is the calculation Chapter 3.6 §6.3 promised.

Three fluids, one running order. ρ∝a−3(1+w)\rho\propto a^{-3(1+w)}ρ∝a−3(1+w) came from one separable equation, and a∝t2/3(1+w)a\propto t^{2/3(1+w)}a∝t2/3(1+w) from another, plus eHΛt\ee^{H_{\Lambda}t}eHΛ​t for the case the formula misses. The three exponents put radiation first, matter second and the cosmological term last, whatever the amounts. The expansion accelerates exactly when w<−13w\lt-\tfrac13w<−31​, which is Chapter 3.6 §5.5's condition unchanged. With the ⚑ measured parameters the universe is 13.8 Gyr13.8\ \mathrm{Gyr}13.8 Gyr old, began accelerating at z=0.63z=0.63z=0.63, and its two best measurements of H0H_{0}H0​ disagree by five times their uncertainty.

The redshift, and what it is not. Following p0p^{0}p0 along a null geodesic gives p0∝1/ap^{0}\propto1/ap0∝1/a and hence 1+z=a0/aem1+z=a_{0}/a_{\text{em}}1+z=a0​/aem​, with no velocity anywhere in the derivation or the answer. Crest-counting gives the same thing by a route sharing no step. Comoving worldlines are geodesics because Γi00=0\Gamma^{i}{}_{00}=0Γi00​=0, so nothing is moving through anything. Proper distances grow as d˙=Hd\dot d=Hdd˙=Hd and exceed ccc beyond 4.45 Gpc4.45\ \mathrm{Gpc}4.45 Gpc, which contradicts nothing because velocities at different points live in different tangent spaces. The balloon is right about having no centre and wrong about the room it sits in.

And the thesis. A conserved energy is the output of Noether's theorem. Its input is a symmetry. In a curved spacetime that symmetry is a timelike Killing vector, and there is none here, because a Killing flow preserves every geometric scalar while R=−8πGc2(ρ−3p/c2)R=-\tfrac{8\pi G}{c^{2}}(\rho-3p/c^{2})R=−c28πG​(ρ−3p/c2) changes with time whenever anything dilutes. So the theorem returns nothing, and 99.91%99.91\%99.91% of the microwave background's energy has gone since last scattering with nothing holding it. What survives is ∇μTμν=0\nabla_{\mu}T^{\mu\nu}=0∇μ​Tμν=0, which in this spacetime is the fluid equation. What obstructs adding it up is the term 3(a′/a)p3(a'/a)p3(a′/a)p, and the fact that ν\nuν is a free index. Three chapters wrote this down in advance, and all three are now paid.

Where this gets spent. Part III is finished, and here is what it built. Gravity is not a force but the shape of the arena. Matter tells geometry how to bend, by Gμν=8πGTμν/c4G_{\mu\nu}=8\pi GT_{\mu\nu}/c^{4}Gμν​=8πGTμν​/c4, and geometry tells matter to move on geodesics. Those two statements have been checked against Mercury's 43′′43''43′′, starlight's 1.75′′1.75''1.75′′, a satellite clock's 38.5 μs38.5\ \mu\mathrm{s}38.5 μs a day, and the expansion of the universe.

Two things are left unpaid on purpose. The first is ⚑ S=A/4S=A/4S=A/4 in Planck units, the entropy of the surface Chapter 3.8 built. It is an area where every other entropy in physics is a volume, it contains ℏ\hbarℏ and GGG together, and general relativity's own answer for it is zero. Chapter 7.9 collects it by counting states in string theory.

The second is the smaller debt, stated in §7.3 rather than apologised for later. Parts IV, V and VI are done on flat spacetime, because the curvature near anything a laboratory holds distorts an atom by five parts in 104410^{44}1044, thirty orders of magnitude below the precision of the best measurement in physics. Gravity returns in Chapter 7.1, at the four places §7.3 named where flatness stops being a good approximation and this part's equations report the edge of their own validity. Part IV begins where Chapter 0.5 left off, and it will need every symmetry argument you have made here.
